resources.string: Ask them for their username and type it here. Once they accept, you can both send each other items: one invitation connects you both ways.
No account currently uses that username.
You are already connected to that account, or have an invitation pending with it. One connection works in both directions.
Nothing can be sent through a connection to this account right now.
Anything you send can be copied by the person you send it to. Only share with people you would trust with the contents.
Disconnecting deletes every share between you, in both directions.
Check their fingerprint before you accept

Read this code to them out loud, on a call or in person, and check it matches what they see. It is the fingerprint of their account key, which never changes. It is the one part of sharing that maths cannot do for you: if the server ever substituted another account for theirs, this is where it shows.
Yours, to read back to them

This connection’s account key is not the one you first checked. An account key never changes, so someone may be intercepting it, and nothing more can be sent through it. Tell them through another channel, then disconnect and invite each other again.
Their sharing keys could not be traced back to their account key, so they may not be theirs. Nothing can be sent through this connection until they can.

The username on this connection now leads to a different account from the one you connected to, so nothing more can be sent through it. This connection is gone. To share again, send a new invitation and compare fingerprints again. A connection is never repaired by looking their username up again: the name may belong to someone else now.

This connection’s keys could not be checked, so nothing can be sent through it right now. This connection is gone. To share again, send a new invitation and compare fingerprints again. A connection is never repaired by looking their username up again: the name may belong to someone else now.
This connection has not been accepted yet, so nothing can be sent through it.
Only you see it. It is sealed in your address book, never sent in the clear.
Every item you shared with each other stops being shared, in both directions. Copies that were already made stay with whoever made them. To share again you both compare fingerprints again.
Nothing is shared yet. Once someone accepts your invitation, or you accept theirs, a folder for the two of you appears here.
Nothing here yet. Anything either of you shares with the other appears in this folder, and you can both organise it into folders.
This phone does not hold the sharing key, so the folders inside this space are not shown. Everything shared with you is listed here instead.
The folders in this space could not be shown safely, so everything is listed at the top level. Resetting removes the folders for both of you; nothing is unshared.
Deleting “%1$s” and the folders inside it removes them for both of you. Everything filed in them moves to the top of this shared space; nothing is unshared.
This item could not be opened.
Shared documents cannot be opened here yet. Everything needed to decrypt this one has arrived; the reader has not been built.
A copy is re-encrypted under a key of your own, so it survives the original being deleted or unshared. Anything you can read can be copied like this, which is why sharing never claims otherwise.
Copied to your account. Your copy is independent of theirs.
This file is too large to copy on this phone. Download it instead.
Your storage does not have room for this, so it was not copied.
The saved file is not encrypted: anything on this phone can read it.
This space could not be read.
Folders go at most 8 levels deep, and that move would go deeper.
A folder cannot go inside itself or one of its own folders.
That folder was removed in the meantime, probably by the other person.
That folder name cannot be used here.
Sent to %1$s, but it could not be put in that folder, so it is at the top of your shared space.
This connection cannot carry this kind of item from this phone yet.
